title: More Apps, Faster Hot-Launch on Mobile Devices via Fore/Background-aware GC-Swap Co-design
problem: Existing methods to cache more apps in mobile device backgrounds using swap degrade hot-launch performance, creating a conflict between capacity and performance. The fundamental challenge is that reducing heap size or aggressive caching hurts the performance of launching cached apps.
motivation: Faster app launching is critical for mobile user experience, and hot-launching from background cache significantly outperforms cold launches from scratch.
method: Fleet is a garbage collector that distinguishes between active and cached app data. It only cleans up cached-app data, leaving active-app data untouched for fast performance. It predicts which data each cached app will need upon launch and uses this to guide how the operating system arranges disk-based memory (called swap). Finally, it groups small data objects with similar access patterns into the same memory pages, improving swap efficiency.
key_novelty: Fleet coordinates garbage collection and memory swapping (disk-based overflow) with active and cached app awareness, simultaneously improving both app caching capacity and hot-launch performance.
contributions: Foreground/background-aware GC design that limits tracing to background objects to avoid interfering with hot-launch performance
Runtime-informed swap guidance that identifies hot-launch critical objects for optimized memory management
Object aggregation technique that groups small objects with similar access patterns to improve swap efficiency
AOSP implementation achieving 1.59× faster hot-launch time and 1.21× more cached apps
primary_theme: Mobile app performance via GC-swap co-design
